title: C213 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
I read this connector like a mixing desk: speaker, microphone, lighting and communication circuits share the panel, but each channel keeps its own identity. Start with the connector identification and the face's harness heading, then use the drawing's cavity labels to find the matching table rows. Wire color is a useful cross-check, but repeated colors make it a lousy solo navigator.

As displayed, the drawing has an outer column at the right, paired columns through the center and an outer column at the left. Gaps and rectangular housing features separate groups; follow the printed labels rather than assuming an uninterrupted grid. Read Circuit Number, Color, Function and Qualifier together. Preserve the positive and negative labels on audio, microphone and video entries, and keep equipment alternatives intact. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in both drawings. That count discrepancy and the overlapping, unqualified speaker assignments remain unresolved; retain the printed entries without choosing a correction.

This reference identifies recorded connections. It does not establish vehicle access, physical viewing direction, release movements or a diagnostic test. The Gauge convention and the Size and Used codes are undefined here and should not become wire-selection instructions. After identifying a circuit, use its applicable diagnostic or service procedure for the next action.

edits.why: The face and harness labels keep the illustration associated with its own hardware record. I use the outline and projections as housing landmarks without assigning them locking or release functions. Neither the MALE label nor the drawing's displayed position establishes which direction to view the installed connector.

The cavity label is the bridge between the illustration and the circuit table. Gray-filled positions should be checked against their rows rather than interpreted as faults. Polarity and equipment wording distinguish circuits that may otherwise look similar. A relay label describes an electrically controlled switching function without proving that a separate plug-in relay exists; LIN identifies a message-carrying connection. Competing audio rows remain unresolved, so this reference cannot select between them.

Read this drawing separately. Its outer columns and paired central columns are reversed left-to-right relative to the male drawing, and its own gray-filled positions must be checked against its own table. These are displayed housing landmarks, not installed viewing-side or release instructions.

Keep the female table’s own colors, gauges and terminal records. Its antenna-power and roof-down gauge alternatives and network-low color alternatives are unqualified. The competing right-front-door woofer and right-middle-speaker assignments remain separate on both faces. The male active-exhaust entry faces a blank female row, so matching cavity labels do not establish a complete physical wiring configuration. Do not select a wire, terminal or test from these unresolved alternatives.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata gives Pin Count 42, while the supplied male-face illustration labels cavities 1 through 40. Confirm the relationship between the recorded count and the illustrated face; neither has been corrected.

Cavity 35 has separate unqualified assignments: RME10 for the right front door woofer negative connection and RME16 for the right middle speaker negative connection, with different colors and terminal part numbers. Confirm whether an equipment qualifier is missing or an entry is incorrect before selecting an assignment.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 115 primary units, six complete pages/two figures and four edits. Original first CLI author covered 55 units/two male headings. Complete draft includes both connector faces and discloses count and assignment discrepancies. Original partial author retained separately; physical count, color, gauge and assignment alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
